title: Global dimension is tested on finite modules and on cyclic modules
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $n\ge0$ an integer. The following are equivalent [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]: (1) $R$ has global dimension $\le n$, i.e. every $R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le n$; (2) every finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] has a projective resolution of length $\le n$; (3) for every ideal $I\subseteq R$ the cyclic $R$-module $R/I$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065T (lemma-finite-gl-dim, line 26856), whose proof uses Lemma lemma-colimit-projective-dimension (line 26800)

proof.text: ((1) $\Rightarrow$ (2) $\Rightarrow$ (3).) By [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], (1) says that every $R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le n$; in particular every finite $R$-module does, which is (2). For an ideal $I\subseteq R$ the module $R/I$ is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]: every element $\bar r=r\cdot\bar1$ is an $R$-multiple of the single generator $\bar1$. So (2) gives (3).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 065T (lemma-finite-gl-dim), line 26866: 'It is clear that (1) => (2) and (2) => (3)'

proof.text: ((3) $\Rightarrow$ (1): a well-ordered filtration.) Assume (3) and let $M$ be any $R$-module. Let $E\subseteq M$ be a set of generators of $M$ (for instance $E=M$). By the well-ordering theorem [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem] choose a well-ordering $\le$ of $E$. For $e\in E$ let $M_e\subseteq M$ be the submodule generated by $\{e'\in E: e'\le e\}$, and $M_{<e}=\bigcup_{e'<e}M_{e'}$ ($=0$ if $e$ is least). If $e'\le e$ then $\{e''\le e'\}\subseteq\{e''\le e\}$, so $M_{e'}\subseteq M_e$. Since $e\in M_e$ and $E$ generates $M$, every element of $M$ is a finite combination $\sum_j a_je_j$, which lies in $M_{e_{\max}}$ for the largest $e_j$ (the $M_e$ form a chain); hence $M=\bigcup_{e\in E}M_e$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 065T, lines 26867-26870

proof.text: (The successive quotients are cyclic.) Fix $e\in E$. The set $\{e'\le e\}$ is $\{e\}\cup\{e'<e\}$, and every $e'<e$ lies in $M_{e'}\subseteq M_{<e}$, while $M_{<e}\subseteq M_e$; so $M_e=Re+M_{<e}$ and the quotient $Q_e=M_e/M_{<e}$ is generated by the class $\bar e$ of $e$ (it is $0$ when $e\in M_{<e}$). The $R$-linear map $\varphi:R\to Q_e$, $r\mapsto r\bar e$, is therefore surjective; with $I=\ker\varphi=\{r\in R: re\in M_{<e}\}$, an ideal of $R$, it induces an isomorphism $\bar\varphi:R/I\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_e$ (first isomorphism theorem). By (3), $R/I$ has a projective resolution $0\to P_n\to\dots\to P_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}R/I\to0$ of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]; replacing $\varepsilon$ by $\bar\varphi\circ\varepsilon$ gives an exact sequence $0\to P_n\to\dots\to P_0\to Q_e\to0$ (composing with an isomorphism keeps surjectivity and the kernel), i.e. a projective resolution of $Q_e$ of length $\le n$. (This includes $Q_e=0$, which is $R/R$.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 065T, lines 26871-26876 ('is either zero or generated by one element, hence has projective dimension <= n by (3)')

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By Steps 2 and 3, $E$ with its well-ordering and the submodules $(M_e)_{e\in E}$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordered-union-projective-dimension] (Stacks 0D1U): $M_{e'}\subseteq M_e$ for $e'\le e$, $M=\bigcup_eM_e$, and every $M_e/M_{<e}$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$. Hence $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$. As $M$ was arbitrary, every $R$-module has one, which is (1) [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Together with Step 1 the three conditions are equivalent.
